_comment: How the broadcast forum activity digest becomes one user's badge, and what the connect header's forum slot carries. The document is one anonymous array of unread counts, identical for every client; only the installation knows its own slot, so every client indexes the same way. Written against the behaviour at HEAD; the readers and the skip lists are described in README.md.

unread_for_slot_cases.name: no_document_is_no_badge
unread_for_slot_cases._comment: A fetch that could not refresh drops the document. Reading that gap as zero would announce as new whatever the user had already seen once it came back.

unread_for_slot_cases.name: a_slot_past_the_published_document_is_no_badge
unread_for_slot_cases._comment: The normal state of an account registered since the last server rebuild.

header_button_cases.name: a_wallet_with_no_forum_account_gets_the_lifebuoy
header_button_cases._comment: The bell would be inert for them, and the forum is where an account comes from.

wording_cases.name: a_saturated_count_is_stated_as_more_than_what_can_be_measured
wording_cases._comment: One digest character per slot, so the count stops climbing at its ceiling; saying 15 there would be a number the user can check and find wrong.

monitor_cases.name: the_count_already_waiting_at_start_gets_the_badge_but_no_notification
monitor_cases._comment: Otherwise every relaunch re-announces the same notifications.

monitor_cases.name: a_lost_document_is_unknown_not_zero
monitor_cases._comment: The gap drops the badge, but the watermark is kept, so the same five come back without being announced as new.

monitor_cases.name: what_the_panel_proved_beats_a_digest_that_has_not_caught_up
monitor_cases._comment: The document is up to a server refresh plus a client poll behind, so the badge would otherwise sit on a stale number for minutes after the user read the panel.

monitor_cases.name: a_changed_document_takes_the_badge_back_from_the_observation
monitor_cases._comment: The panel read left nothing unread, so two in a later document is activity that arrived after it and is announced as such.

monitor_cases.name: another_account_starts_from_nothing_known
monitor_cases._comment: Its predecessor's count says nothing about it, and neither does what the app observed for the previous one.

monitor_cases.name: turning_the_setting_back_on_does_not_announce_what_happened_meanwhile
monitor_cases._comment: The watermark advances even while the setting is off.
